01 The process

From limit
to reminder.

A small process on your machine.
A reminder that survives a restart.

  1. Codex / Claude Code

    Read the window.

    Reads Codex through your local sign-in, or Claude through its status line. No inference requests.

    01
  2. SQLite / local state

    Save the reminder.

    An exhausted window creates a saved alert. Pending reminders resume when the watcher restarts.

    02
  3. Reset time / fresh check

    Check once more.

    At the recorded reset it checks Codex allowance when available. Claude reminders use the saved reset time and stay expected-only.

    03
  4. Resend / your inbox

    Send the context.

    The email says whether the reset is expected or fresh data confirms available allowance.

    04

02 Installation

Set it up.
Then step away.

Build from source, choose your providers,
and let setup guide you.

Source on GitHub ↗
01

Clone & build.

In PowerShell or Command Prompt, open the folder that should hold ResetWatch. Requires Git and Go 1.27.2 or newer.

Keep this folder, or move the binary to a directory on your PATH.

PowerShell / CMD
git clone https://github.com/ph03iA/resetwatch.git
cd resetwatch
go build ./cmd/resetwatch
.\resetwatch.exe version
02

Run guided setup.

Choose Codex, Claude, or both. Setup asks for your reminder email and sender, and securely prompts for a missing Resend key.

Claude already has a custom status line? Setup asks before replacing it and saves the original entry.

Codex needs a subscription sign-in. If prompted, run codex login and retry.

Guided setup
.\resetwatch.exe setup
03

Start the watcher.

Run from the folder where setup saved your .env. ResetWatch keeps your chosen providers and reminder settings locally.

Rerun setup to change providers. Changes apply on the next cycle; changing the API key requires a restart.

Start watching
.\resetwatch.exe watch

Keep the watcher running on an awake, online machine. Ctrl + C stops it safely.

03 Operating notes

The details,
up front.

A small tool with clear boundaries.
Read these before relying on an alert.

Read the source ↗
Setup & choice
Choose Codex, Claude, or both in guided setup. A missing key is saved in this folder’s .env. Deselecting a provider cancels its unsent reminders.
Uptime
Keep the watcher running on an awake, online computer. An always-on host needs its own Codex sign-in. There is no hosted scheduler.
Supported sign-in
Codex with a ChatGPT subscription, or Claude Pro/Max through Claude Code’s status line. API-key-only accounts do not expose the supported plan limits.
Your data
Quota snapshots, settings and alert history stay locally. Your recipient, sender and alert content go to Resend. The API key is read from your local .env file or environment, never saved in the database.
Reset evidence
Claude reminders describe expected resets. Codex confirmation requires fresh backend permission and allowance in every reported window. A reset time alone never proves access.
Delivery & retries
A delivered alert means Resend accepted it; inbox placement is not guaranteed. Retries reuse one message key within bounded limits. Reset alerts older than 24 hours are cancelled.
Account switches
One Codex account per state directory. Same-email workspace switches cannot be reliably distinguished; check quota after switching.
